text.p: Volatile copper trading dominated LME trading on Monday, while gold, wheat and oil prices all eased. The CRB index ended down 2.03 at 246.24.
Copper trading remained volatile during Monday afternoon trading on the LME, as an extreme technical squeeze on nearby supplies unravelled viciously.

The cash/threes backwardation, which stood at $210 at one stage, narrowed to $87/97 at the close, as waves of lending knocked the stuffing out of the market, pulling forward prices down in their wake.
"This market is totally confused...but the short-term fundamentals are supportive, which is playing into the hands of the longs," said Angus MacMillan, analyst at LME broker Billiton Metals Ltd.

The squeeze is taking place against a background of supply disputes in Chile, the world's largest producer, falling global stocks, and a temporary closure of the big Kennecott smelter in the U.S. Traders said that this has coincided with major short positions falling due.
"There is a big short that keeps on getting rolled forward. It happened at the end of October, January, end-April, and is now being pushed to the end of July," one said.

Three months prices, meanwhile, were nervy after hitting an early peak of $2,407, and fell rapidly as the spreads collapsed. By the end of the kerb the market was at $2,356, down $27 from Friday's kerb close.
Prices held just above the $2,350 level, but today's technical action and close is poor, which suggests that the downside will be tested again.
Despite the wide price moves and the extent of the backwardation contraction, volumes and liquidity were not large in copper.

Business in other metals was also not significant, although aluminium was an exception, building constructively above $1,600 against a background of technical tightness in early July, belived to reflect fund covering.
Although prices were unable to clear $1,640, last trade at $1,628.50 was still $15.50 up from the previous kerb.
Lead and zinc turned tail from steadier levels, and finished at $630 and $1,267, down $1 and $8 respectively.
Nickel closed $20 easier at $7,460, while tin was down $10 at $5,730. Alloy was indicated at $1,505/15.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals ended lower as options expired, with white metals sharply weaker, partly on talk that Russia would settle a debt by supplying platinum and palladium, traders said. A continuing strong performance by the dollar against the mark and yen also discouraged investment in precious metals, traders said. COMEX June gold settled $2.50 weaker at $341.40 an ounce, traded $343.30 to $340.50. Bullion was quoted by dealers at $339.30/$339.80.

CBOT wheat futures closed lower on improved crop weather in the U.S. and in European wheat growing regions including France. Wheat closed four to 12 cents per bushel lower, with May down 11-1/2 at $4.12 bushel.

Crude oil futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) edged lower in very thin trade Monday as the market struggled to find direction. Front-month June crude, having traded within a narrow range, settled eight cents lower at $19.91 a barrel. Political violence in Nigeria's Warri oil-producing region has kept a floor under prices but the disruption has not been enough to lift an oversupplied market, traders said.

CSCE world sugar futures closed weaker and within their recent trading range ahead of the May contract's expiry Wednesday, dealers said. The most-active month finished down 0.07 cent at 11.07 cents after trading from 11.12 to 11.01 cents. Spot May eased 0.06 to 11.49, while the back months ended 0.06 to 0.03 lower.
